$comment: Canonical wire-protocol fixtures for the mobile tunnel (#240 / #46 / #2497 = contract v2; v3 adds audio_frame; v4 adds session_wake + session_wake_result; v5 adds set_push_token; v6 adds jobs_set_status; v7 adds node_body_request + node_body). Shared BYTE-IDENTICALLY by base-studio-code (Rust serde tests in src-tauri/src/mobile/tunnel/tests.rs resolve this file by name; PLUS the TS test carried on the `tunnel.ts` RECORD, which the gate emits to .bsc-records/features/tunnel/lib/tunnel.test.tsx and runs there — it is NOT a file under src/, so `ls` and a grep scoped to src/ will both report it missing when it is in fact live) and by mobile-studio-code (src/lib/tunnel/tunnelProtocol.fixtures.test.ts, which decodes EVERY case and throws on an unmodelled type — so adding a case here obliges a matching TunnelClientMessage member and decoder arm in that repo, in the same change). These application frames are carried UNCHANGED inside the relay's Noise-encrypted envelope ({room, ciphertext}) — the Cloudflare relay never sees them in plaintext. Messages are flat JSON tagged by a snake_case `type`; multi-word field names are camelCase. Contract v2 adds: auth/auth_ok protocolVersion, the generic store_state projection frame, the optional PaneDescriptor.kind, and pins the plan_sync frames to the Rust (bsc-tunnel) shapes. #2511 rides WITHIN v2 (additive, no version bump): auth_ok.inputGranted (always serialized by the current desktop; optional for mobile — auth_ok_pre_grant pins the pre-#2511 shape) + the input_grant_changed broadcast. #3757 also rides within v2 (additive): store_state_chunk fragments an over-cap store_state domain across Noise messages (each chunk a raw UTF-8 slice of the json, seq 0..total), which mobile reassembles by (domain, rev) and applies as a store_state — an older mobile ignores the unknown type.

pairing.$comment: The pairing payload the desktop shows as a QR, in BOTH encodings the phone accepts. `canonical` is the historical JSON form. `compact` packs the same four fields into QR ALPHANUMERIC mode (uppercase base32 + a `*` separator, all inside the 45-character alphanumeric set) so the code needs version 6 / 41x41 modules instead of version 10 / 57x57 at EC level M — MEASURED on the live payload. THE QR IS ONLY A TRANSPORT: `compact` carries RAW BYTES and the phone re-derives `canonical` exactly, so the relay's room-id validation (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$/), the Noise IK handshake and the constant-time psk comparison are all untouched and no wire frame changes. The separator is `*` because it is alphanumeric-safe and can appear in neither a hostname nor base32's A-Z2-7 — `.` would have collided with the host's own dots. The `https://` scheme is dropped because the phone's normalizeRelayUrl rewrites it to `wss://` on arrival anyway; `normalizedRelayUrl` is what a decode must produce. Uppercasing is lossless for a hostname but NOT for a URL path, so an encoder must refuse the compact form when the relay URL carries one and emit JSON instead. NOTE this section is a SIBLING of serverToClient/clientToServer and is not a wire frame: the Rust serde test indexes those two keys explicitly and the mobile fixtures test destructures only those two, so adding it obliges no TunnelClientMessage member or decoder arm.

pairingV2.$comment: ONE PAIRING, EVERY ROOM (one-pairing-assigns-every-room). The QR carries a SEED instead of a room id and a psk; each host derives its own pair from it, so pairing once reaches every feature and adding a feature later costs nothing on the wire and no re-pairing. room(f) = base64url(HMAC-SHA256(seed, 'room:'+f)[0..24]) — 32 chars, satisfying the relay's ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$ and identical in shape to a rolled id. psk(f) = hex(HMAC-SHA256(seed, 'psk:'+f)) — 64 lowercase hex, the exact shape the desktop's constant-time comparison expects. The `room:` / `psk:` prefixes are DOMAIN SEPARATION: without them a feature's room and secret would be two views of one digest. FEATURE NAMES ARE WIRE CONSTANTS and map to HOSTS, not message types — the relay allows one host per room, which is why rooms exist at all rather than one multiplexed channel. The compact line is B2*<HOST>*<PK>*<SEED>, 150 chars against B1's 190 — QR version 5 (37x37) instead of 6 (41x41), MEASURED. B1 and the JSON form stay accepted: an un-updated desktop must still pair.
pairingV2.$lanComment: LAN FIRST, RELAY SECOND (the-phone-reaches-the-host-over-the-lan-first). An optional FIFTH part carries the host's LAN address, uppercased like the relay host: B2*<HOST>*<PK>*<SEED>*<LAN>. The phone dials ws://<lan>:<port>/connect?room=<room(f)>&role=guest first and silently falls back to the relay. PORTS ARE WIRE CONSTANTS per feature, exactly as the feature names are - each feature is a different host PROCESS, so each needs its own listener - which is why no port rides in the QR. The 4-part form stays valid: a host with no LAN address simply omits the part.
